The key to understanding this situation is to look at the Julia set for the parabolic root
points. Since the two root points of an A component are dual to each other, they have Julia
sets which are identical, except for the choice of which component to label as a and which
to label as −a .
Nearly all of the examples we know are for rabbit regions. As one specific example, let
us concentrate on the 1/3 -rabbit region as shown in Figure 54, and on the A component
in the upper left of this Figure. Figure 60 illustrates the Julia set for either of its two root
points. (See Figure 21 for an analogous Julia set for the 1/2 rabbit, and Figure 23 for the
1/5 rabbit.)
Given any co-periodic angle θ with denominator 3(3p −1) , it is useful to consider the
corresponding periodic angle 3θ with denominator 3p −1 . Note that two co-periodic angles
θ and θ′ satisfy 3θ = 3θ′ if and only if they are twins.
In our example, the root point of each ±2a component in the Julia set is the landing point
of six dynamic rays. However, only four of the six dynamic angles correspond to parameter
angles for rays landing at the specified root point of A. Below is a table describing the
angles for the six dynamic rays landing at the left hand root point in Figure 54 (or 60), and
